channel: securities issued for acquired assets instead of cash
why_tested: no cash to buy the plants
cost_or_effort: $13161813 of net worth acquired for cash $6127668 plus preferred and common paper
result: nine-plus makes assembled, eight of them later abandoned
repeatability: proven repeatable for small makers, unproven for large prizes (Ford, Maxwell)
notes: the operating channel of Stage 1 was the exchange of securities

channel: first-lien note issue with a stock bonus
why_tested: funding need after the 1909 cash failures
cost_or_effort: $15000000 priced at 96 with a 20 per cent stock bonus
result: fully sold in advance of public offering
repeatability: repeatable only by surrendering board control via the voting trust

channel: open-market equity accumulation as a control channel
cost_or_effort: purchases with Du Pont and Kaufman; price 82 to high 558
result: nearly a clear board majority; chairmanship to Du Pont

channel: underwritten public offering of a Durant-sponsored make
why_tested: funding output from 100 to 300 cars a day
result: taken up; 'numerous motor-car dealers and General Motors stockholders' subscribed on Durant's name
repeatability: repeatable: rerun in 1916-05 with United Motors at $62
notes: the name itself was the distribution asset

channel: captive supply contract as a channel
why_tested: body supply for a multi-make portfolio
cost_or_effort: cost plus 17.6 per cent to Fisher, alongside a 60 per cent equity purchase
result: supplier profits large enough to make the minority reluctant to sell in 1926
repeatability: not repeatable as a bargain: resolved by absorption
